newsitem.title: USA: Maker of ZIG-ZAG papers to roll out junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Maker of ZIG-ZAG papers to roll out junk bonds.

text.p: Holy smokes! Investors looking to satisfy their craving for junk bonds will have a chance to buy a new issue from a company whose main products will be Beech-Nut chewing tobacco and ZIG-ZAG rolling papers.

National Tobacco Co LP, the third-largest marketer of loose leaf chewing tobacco in the U.S., is in the process of buying North Atlantic Trading Co Inc, the leader in "roll-your-own" cigarette papers with a 49 percent U.S. market share.
The new company, to be called North American Trading Co Inc, plans to raise around $115 million in the junk bond market to finance the acquisition and refinance existing debt.
NatWest Securities Corp and CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp will underwrite the private placement of seven-year senior notes.
Price talk on the notes, which have been rated B3/B-plus, is 11 percent to 11 1/4 percent. The deal is expected to price this Thursday.

The deal's underwriters are downplaying the risks associated with investing in a tobacco products company in the current atmosphere of anti-tobacco fervor. Company officials did not return phone calls.

Investment banking officials, who asked not to be quoted by name, acknowledged that smokeless tobacco companies may be required to bear a share of the burden of any sweeping liabilty settlements. But they said their hypothetical projections show any likely settlement costs would be small enough for the company to pass along to consumers without significantly hurting sales.

They pointed out that to date, National Tobacco has never lost or settled a lawsuit claiming that using chewing tobacco causes disease. Moreover, investment bank officials pointed to the lucrative nature of the chewing tobacco and rolling paper businesses.
Both Beech-Nut chewing tobacco and Zig-Zag rolling papers offer high profit margins and consistent cash flows, experts said. The brands also generate strong customer loyalty.

Moody's reported that the overall market for chewing tobacco has declined two percent in each of the past five years, and the drop is expected to continue. But National Tobacco has managed to gain overall market share by developing new products catering to niche customers.
After the merger, the new company will have a more diverse revenue base and should benefit from cross-marketing synergies for its major products, experts said.
Sources close to the deal said Wall Street's wariness about tobacco investments might actually benefit investors who are willing to buy the bonds.

"There are some accounts that have restrictions on investments in tobacco-related companies. So investors in this deal will get paid a premium given the fact that this is tobacco company," said a market source.
